## Scientific questions still open {#next-tests}

The most immediate computational check for stellar visibility is Izar at 60° N. Trace the high-latitude evening visibility boundary against the published inputs and investigate the treatment of shallow twilight. The discrepancy is about five days. [Published-reference comparison](heliacal-rising.qmd#published-reference-calculations).

Other checks that can use existing reference material include frame and parallax conventions in A03, independent projection and constellation geometry in V06, and sky brightness against archival imagery or photometry in V02–V04. The current sky-step result applies to native frames. A comparison with Stellarium would need a controlled external capture. The observational extensions of H05 and F01 require independently surveyed controls.
